paragraphs: One-sentence assessment | This career is worth exploring further only if you are willing to use engineering and physics to address extremely high-risk nuclear safety issues with personal accountability, repeatedly verify evidence across design, operational monitoring and compliance judgments, and accept regulatory review and formal recordkeeping requirements.

Core output | Connect design bases, safety analyses, operational monitoring data, compliance judgments and response recommendations into traceable technical documents: design or modification proposals, safety analysis reports, operating procedures, monitoring and event reports, and explanatory materials for regulators, rather than just a conclusion.

20—120-minute safe trial | Conduct an off-site exercise using a fictional scenario: draw an event timeline for a hypothetical abnormal operating condition, list three monitoring parameters that must be checked and two judgment criteria requiring escalation, and draft a table of contents for a one-page technical explanation. Do not use this exercise to make operating, reactor shutdown or compliance conclusions about any real facility.

First hurdle | Verify authorization boundaries first: who may decide operation and reactor shutdown, sign safety analyses and hold an operator license. US nuclear engineers typically do not need licensure to enter the occupation, but reactor operator licenses are granted by the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission through statutory procedures. In China, special nuclear safety personnel, including civilian nuclear facility operators, registered nuclear safety engineers, welders and nondestructive examination personnel, are subject to qualification licensing under the Nuclear Safety Law and related rules. Registration is not an operator license.

Nuclear engineers (O*NET-SOC 17-2161.00) apply nuclear science and engineering principles to research, design and operations involving nuclear energy and waste: designing reactor cores, radiation shielding, instrumentation and control and related equipment; monitoring facility operations and identifying designs, construction and operations that violate safety regulations or endanger safety; initiating corrective actions or ordering reactor shutdown in emergencies; writing operating procedures and technical reports; contributing to environmental compliance, waste disposal and decommissioning plans; and communicating with regulators, suppliers and nuclear facility review committees.

entries: Design and development | Design or develop nuclear equipment and systems such as reactor cores, radiation shielding, and instrumentation and control equipment.
Operational monitoring and compliance judgments | Monitor nuclear facility operations and identify designs, construction or operating practices that violate safety regulations or may endanger safety.
Emergency response | Initiate corrective actions or issue reactor shutdown orders in emergencies.
Accident investigation and technical analysis | Investigate accidents and obtain data for designing preventive measures; synthesize test results into analyses and recommendations.

Procedures and reports | Write operating instructions for nuclear facilities and nuclear fuel / waste handling and disposal; prepare technical reports, environmental impact statements and presentations.

Fuel and waste, environmental compliance and collaboration | Test fuel behavior and cycles, design processes to reduce radioactive waste, direct environmental compliance activities, and discuss construction and modification proposals with suppliers, contractors or review committees.

paragraphs: Work primarily combines offices and facility sites. O*NET work context data show that 90% use email daily, 65% communicate by telephone daily, 55% have face-to-face discussions daily, and 65% work indoors in controlled conditions daily. Meanwhile, 62% work more than 40 hours per week and 76% have regular schedules.

Accuracy and responsibility for consequences are both high: 71% consider exactness or accuracy extremely important, 40% report extremely serious consequences of errors and 20% very serious consequences. Responsibility for others' health and safety is very high for 38% and high for 29%; 19% face daily radiation exposure and 30% wear common protective equipment daily.

The emphasis is on traceable safety arguments: aligning design assumptions, analytical models, monitoring data and regulatory clauses, and specifying escalation routes when evidence is insufficient or abnormalities arise, rather than relying on experience alone for conclusions.

Quality is measured by traceable design bases and safety analyses, complete monitoring data and deviation handling, clear applicable regulatory clauses, abnormalities and events reported and resolved under procedures, and reviewed and approved changes, rather than schedule or cost alone.

Responsibility boundaries | Education, professional registration, role qualification licensing and operating authorization are distinct statuses. Nuclear engineers may handle design, analysis and technical support, but operating and reactor shutdown decisions typically rest with licensed operators and facility management. A registered nuclear safety engineer certificate is not a reactor operator license; no qualification removes institutional safety responsibility or regulatory review.

The workflow proceeds as follows: requirements and safety objectives → design and safety analysis → review and approval → construction or modification and commissioning → operational monitoring and deviation handling → event reporting, operating experience feedback and continuous improvement. Occupational boundaries | This occupation is distinct from nuclear facility operators, nuclear monitoring technicians and nondestructive examination personnel. Operation, on-site monitoring and inspection each have separate qualifications and authorization.

Nuclear facility operators | Center their work on reactor operations and fault response and require regulator-issued licenses. This occupation handles design, safety analysis and technical support and typically does not directly operate reactors.

Nuclear monitoring technicians and nuclear technicians | Handle instrument monitoring, sample measurements and on-site technical support, without responsibility for preparing or signing safety analysis reports. Nuclear safety equipment nondestructive examination personnel perform inspections according to qualification levels and do not reach compliance conclusions on facility operation.

Selection signal | Compare more than the fact that all these occupations work in the nuclear industry. Consider who decides operation and reactor shutdown, who signs safety analyses, and whether starting the role requires an operator license or professional registration.
Centers on on-site operation and fault response, bears direct responsibility for operational safety, and requires a regulator-issued license.

Consider operator work if you prefer long-term shift operations and unit operation and are willing to pass licensing assessments. Consider this occupation if you prefer design, analysis and regulatory communication.

Start with tasks | Task exposure to generative AI does not equal actual adoption, the probability of automation or job disappearance. This page analyzes tasks and work contexts from O*NET 17-2161.00 individually and does not invent a replacement rate or score for this occupation.

Potential assistance (editorial analysis) | In authorized settings, assistance with technical document drafts, standards searches, record organization and code drafts may be evaluated. This review did not obtain occupational deployment, accuracy or safety calculation validation evidence; Hot Technologies does not provide such proof.

Candidate calculation scripts | Generated code requires checks of model assumptions, units, boundaries and validation. Specialized simulation calculations do not establish generative AI reliability; unvalidated results cannot be used directly for safety conclusions.

Candidate data checks | Verify rule-based alarms, trend analysis and generative AI separately. Actual deployment effects were not obtained; abnormal operating conditions, instrument status and safety impacts require review by responsible personnel.

Authorized personnel remain responsible for safety conclusions, change approval, report signatures and emergency decisions under license conditions and institutional responsibilities. Verify licensing separately for control system operation and supervision; not every engineering decision equates to operator licensing.

Human control points | Verify input data and model versions, confirm applicable regulatory clauses, review calculation results and safety margins, and have authorized personnel sign and implement escalation and reporting procedures.

First verify data classification, contracts and system authorization. Handle confidential facility / nuclear material / national defense information under applicable rules; public teaching models are not uniformly controlled. Do not upload unauthorized information; humans must review outputs and retain records.

Capability development | Build expertise in reactor physics and thermal hydraulics, safety analysis and probabilistic safety assessment, application of regulations and standards, abnormal operating condition judgments and regulatory communication, beyond generating documents faster.

This is the US O*NET17-2161 occupation. This review did not verify a one-to-one Chinese classification / qualification mapping. China's special nuclear safety personnel include operators, registered nuclear safety engineers, civilian nuclear safety equipment welders and nondestructive examination personnel, each managed separately. This does not mean all nuclear engineering design roles uniformly require any one of these certificates.

Definition comparison | The National Bureau of Statistics publishes average wages of employees in urban units by industry section, without listing nuclear engineers separately. This page uses electricity, heat, gas and water production and supply industry-section averages as a reference, alongside scientific research and technical services averages.

Verifiable reference | In 2025, average annual wages for employees in urban nonprivate units in electricity, heat, gas and water production and supply were RMB 160,897, compared with RMB 66,451 in urban private units in the same industry. Scientific research and technical services averages were RMB 182,064 for nonprivate units and RMB 83,560 for private units. Coverage includes legal entities in urban areas with 5 or more employees; individually owned businesses and freelancers are excluded.

Insufficient evidence: this review did not obtain nationwide Chinese occupational wages on a comparable basis. Industry averages serve only as references for related nuclear power operation and engineering technical service employers and do not establish occupational medians. Verify registered nuclear safety engineer examination education / experience requirements and four subjects against the 2026 notice. Passing the examination, practicing under the registered title after registration, and institutional authorization require separate verification.

The 2025 BLS OEWS data displayed by O*NET report the exact occupation 17-2161.00: median hourly wage of USD 64.41 and median annual wage of USD 133,970. These figures are not starting salaries or individual quoted rates.

National annual wage percentiles under the same definition are USD 92,960 at the 10th percentile, USD 108,690 at the 25th, USD 163,630 at the 75th and USD 196,290 at the 90th. Corresponding hourly wages are USD 44.69, 52.26, 78.67 and 94.37.
The percentiles and medians all use 2025 BLS OEWS national data and cannot be directly compared across years, regions or employer types.

OEWS measures pretax wages for regular working hours and excludes the self-employed and owners and partners of unincorporated businesses. It includes hazard pay, incentives and production bonuses, while excluding overtime premiums, shift differentials and meals and lodging, among other items. It does not categorically exclude all project bonuses.
Lower percentiles are not starting salaries for new graduates or newcomers, and distribution data cannot be used to estimate individual take-home pay or after-tax income.

Compensation structures differ among operating organizations, design institutes, suppliers and regulatory technical support institutions. Verify the specific employer, region and role category. US figures cannot be converted into individual income in mainland China.

paragraphs: Caution signal | You are mainly attracted by the energy industry but are unwilling to bear safety responsibility and compliance pressure, or expect relatively little regulatory constraint as in ordinary engineering roles.

Verification method | Personality and interest labels cannot determine fit. Use a fictional operating condition to practice an event timeline and parameter checks, and obtain evaluation from experienced engineers in a teaching or guided training setting.

Scope statement | This checklist cannot replace nuclear safety regulations, license conditions, institutional safety analysis procedures or emergency plans. Main risks include inapplicable safety analysis assumptions or models, unidentified monitoring abnormalities, insufficient evidence for compliance judgments, failed change control, inadequate radiation protection and on-site work controls, and operating or reactor shutdown decisions beyond authorization. Controls should be tailored to facility license conditions and institutional procedures.

Direct answer | The main risks are safety analyses relying on unconfirmed assumptions, abnormal monitoring data dismissed as instrument faults, treating regulatory minimums as sufficient conditions, design changes bypassing review, and unclear escalation routes in emergencies. Controls depend on independent review, clear safety margins and acceptance criteria, procedural reporting and operating experience feedback, and licensed personnel's operating authorization.

US O*NET figures for accuracy at 71% / extremely serious errors at 40% / very high safety responsibility at 38% / daily radiation exposure at 19% are survey results, not accident rates. NRC operator licensing and China's 2021 operator rules each apply to control system operation; institutional engineering and emergency authority require separate verification. Review controls are editorial recommendations tailored to roles.

Design, safety analysis, compliance and operational safety review teams are all within the responsibility chain. Reactor shutdown recommendations and emergency decisions follow facility authorization; control system operation and supervision require separate licensing checks. Not all decision-making authority equates to operating authority.

Possible consequences | Incorrect safety analyses or unidentified abnormalities may cause equipment damage, radioactive releases and personnel exposure. Missing records and change controls may make safety arguments untraceable and trigger regulatory penalties. Unauthorized operating decisions entail direct safety and legal responsibility.

Step 0: determine jurisdiction and role authorization | First identify the intended country or region and employer type, such as operating organization, design institute, supplier or regulatory technical support institution. Verify education requirements, professional qualifications, role licensing and operating authorization boundaries. The pathway on this page is an editorial synthesis, does not represent uniform entry requirements and does not authorize design, operation or reactor shutdown.
Under guidance, help organize design inputs, review calculations and search references and regulations, while learning institutional change control and document management procedures.
Entry and guided learning stage
Undertake component- or subsystem-level analysis and design within the authorized scope, produce calculation documents and design descriptions, and submit them for review under procedures.
Independent analysis stage

Undertake system-level safety analysis and compliance judgments, participate in design change reviews, event investigations and operating experience feedback, and provide technical materials for regulatory communication.
Systems and safety analysis stage

Lead a technical specialty or professional review, oversee overall consistency of safety arguments, standards implementation and team development, and take responsibility for technical conclusions on major changes.

career_path_block.direct_answer: US O*NET JobZone4, with 81% bachelor's / 19% master's degrees, and BLS's typical related engineering bachelor's degree and on-site training for new employees. Job Zone is not a fixed number of years for everyone. PE is a state engineering license. NCEES administers the nuclear engineering PE examination, but passing does not automatically confer state licensure. BLS states that US entry roles do not require a license; this does not exempt all senior service roles. NRC licenses for operating / supervising control systems are distinct from engineering appointments. China's registered nuclear safety engineer qualifications follow 2026 eligibility requirements. Distinguish examination passage, registration and employer task authorization; registration certificates and engineering degrees cannot replace operator licenses.

components.definition_block: Nuclear engineers (O*NET-SOC 17-2161.00) apply nuclear science and engineering principles to research, design and operations involving nuclear energy and waste: designing reactor cores, radiation shielding, and instrumentation and control equipment; monitoring facility operations and identifying practices that violate safety regulations or endanger safety; initiating corrective actions or ordering reactor shutdown in emergencies; writing operating procedures and safety analysis reports; and participating in environmental compliance and waste disposal. Actual permitted activities depend on education, professional qualifications, role licensing and operating authorization. Distinguish shutdown recommendations, authorized decisions and actual operation; the job title itself does not confer permission to operate control systems.

This career suits people willing to verify assumptions and evidence over time, accept regulatory review and bear responsibility for high-consequence outcomes.

questions.question: What education is required?

questions.answer: PE is a state engineering license. NCEES administers the nuclear engineering PE examination, but passing does not automatically confer state licensure. BLS states that US entry roles do not require a license; this does not exempt all senior service roles. NRC licenses for operating / supervising control systems are distinct from engineering appointments. Chinese professional qualifications for key nuclear safety roles follow applicable frameworks. Verify examination passage, registration and operator licensing separately; do not extend one certificate to all nuclear engineering roles.
questions.question: Which qualifications are needed?

questions.answer: BLS lists a related engineering bachelor's degree as typical. Feasibility for physics or other graduates depends on courses, projects and hiring requirements; working first as a technician or monitor does not promise a natural transition to engineer. China's 2026 registered nuclear safety engineer examination also requires corresponding education and experience for other specialties; examination eligibility is not job acceptance.

description.text: Nuclear engineers (O*NET 17-2161.00) design nuclear equipment and systems, monitor nuclear facility operations, identify safety violations and initiate corrective actions in emergencies, write procedures and safety analysis reports, and participate in environmental compliance and waste disposal. This page explains their tasks, preparation requirements, Chinese and US qualification and regulatory boundaries, and wage and employment definitions.

subject.name: Nuclear engineers
subject.summary: Nuclear engineers (O*NET-SOC 17-2161.00) apply nuclear science and engineering principles to research, design and operations involving nuclear energy and waste: designing reactor cores, radiation shielding, and instrumentation and control equipment; monitoring nuclear facility operations and identifying designs and operations that violate safety regulations or endanger safety; initiating corrective actions or ordering reactor shutdown in emergencies; writing operating procedures and technical reports; participating in environmental compliance, waste disposal and decommissioning plans; and communicating with regulators, suppliers and review committees. This page uses only official sources to explain occupational scope, tasks, preparation requirements, Chinese and US statistical definitions, and authorization boundaries.
